title: 5 email marketing tips to raise campaign ROI: deliverability, mobile, one CTA, segments, subject lines
summary: Ross Jenkins, founder of a digital agency, argues email is among the cheapest and most measurable channels, and lays out five tactical fixes. Watch deliverability first, write for mobile, use one CTA, segment the list, and use humor in subject lines to earn opens.

principles.text: Monitor deliverability first; if emails don't reach the inbox, every other metric is moot.
principles.quote: If nobody is receiving your emails, everything else is irrelevant.

principles.text: Write every email assuming it will be read on a phone: punchy subject, direct copy, responsive design.
principles.quote: When you are writing your email subject lines and copy, assume that all users are going to receive, open and view your message on a mobile device.

principles.text: Give each email one clear call to action so recipients know exactly what to do.
principles.quote: If you want to see your emails convert at a higher rate, include a single call to action, and tell your recipient what that action is and what you want them to do.

principles.text: Segment your list instead of blasting everyone; start with customers vs non-customers and split further from there.
principles.quote: If you are sending the same message to your entire email list, you are missing a huge opportunity and leaving a lot of money on the table every time you deploy a message.

principles.text: The subject line gates all return, so make it stand out and test humor and shock value.
principles.quote: Your subject line needs to command attention and trigger the recipient to click on it.

principles.text: Email is cheap, highly measurable, and can be tuned to outperform other channels, yet most businesses under-invest in it.
principles.quote: Many businesses put very little effort into their email marketing, and it shows.
